short_name: CA SB 79 — Tier 1 TOD stop, within 1/4 mile
statute_citation: Cal. Gov. Code §§ 65912.155–65912.162 (added by Stats. 2025, Ch. 512 (SB 79)); § 65912.157 amended by Stats. 2026, Ch. 100 (SB 722), approved 2026-07-16
statutory_exclusions: calfire_or_state_vhfhsz (very high fire hazard severity zone bars streamlined review under § 65913.4(a)(6)(D), applied through § 65912.159(a)(3); § 65912.157(j) also requires objective fire safety standards)

mobilehome_or_rv_park_site (§ 65912.157(h)(3), added by SB 722: land governed by the Mobilehome Residency Law, Recreational Vehicle Park Occupancy Law, Mobilehome Parks Act or Special Occupancy Parks Act)
summary: Housing development is an allowed use on residential, mixed or commercial sites within 1/4 mile of a Tier 1 transit-oriented development stop (heavy rail or 72+ trains/day commuter rail) in an urban transit county (>15 passenger rail stations). Local governments may not impose a height limit below 75 ft, a density cap below 120 du/acre, or standards precluding a residential FAR of 3.5 (§ 65912.157(a)(3)). Projects need at least 5 units and 30 du/acre. Applies to local agencies from July 1, 2026 (§ 65912.157(n)). The 75 ft / 120 du/ac figures are floors on local limits, not a unit cap. SB 79 does not by itself grant ministerial approval; see § 65912.159 for the streamlining path. Amended by SB 722 (Ch. 100, Stats. 2026, approved 2026-07-16) to exclude sites governed by the mobilehome and RV park laws.

unmapped_condition: 16 or fewer units, and outside the town's conservation and traffic mitigation districts (at most two, together no more than 4% of land area); 17+ units may be required up to 1 space per studio or one-bedroom and 2 per larger unit, or the parking-needs-assessment number if lower
summary: Zoning may not require a minimum number of off-street parking spaces for any residential development except as § 8-3n allows: towns may set minimums for developments over 16 units (and, in up to two small districts, for smaller ones), but if the developer submits a parking needs assessment the requirement cannot exceed 1 space per studio or one-bedroom and 2 per unit with two or more bedrooms, or the assessment's number if lower.

fema_100yr_floodway.note: No flood-zone exclusion in s. 8-2s: it reaches 'any lot that is zoned for commercial or mixed-use development'. s. 8-2s borrows only a definition from s. 8-13hh. The flood language in s. 8-13hh(d) concerns a different thing, what land the State may not require inside a transit-oriented district: 'not require the inclusion of the following lands in any such district: (A) Special flood hazard areas designated on a flood insurance rate map published by the National Flood Insurance Program'. Summary review still allows a finding 'that public health and safety will not be substantially impacted' (s. 8-2r). Read Conn. Gen. Stat. s. 8-2s (a)-(c), s. 8-13hh (a)-(k) and s. 8-2r in full.
